name: Defiance School
district_operator: St. Charles County common school district No. 68; Francis Howell R-III after consolidation
notes: RESOLVED IDENTITY: 'Defiance School' is documented as the popular (not formal) name of Walnut Grove School (District No. 68) — the 1943 Ramsay place-names thesis (State Historical Society of Missouri) says 'Defiance School: See Walnut Grove School' and 'the popular, but not formal name of Defiance School is also given, for the town.' Walnut Grove School was first located near Darst & Levee Roads in Darst Bottom before 1875 (earlier name Sycamore School); about 1944 the building was cut into sections and moved to a hill in Defiance next to the Methodist church cemetery due to flooding (Bob Brail, 'The One-Room Schools of Township 45, Range 2,' Boone-Duden Historical Society sources). The school was still operating in Defiance during the 1948-49 school year (teacher Opal Schemmer, class of 7 boys). No closure date found — neighboring Bacon School closed June 2, 1950 in the same consolidation wave, and Defiance-area students now attend Daniel Boone Elementary (opened 1955 in New Melle, seed row ALL-587 researched in batch 19) per Wikipedia's Defiance article; closure likely fell in the 1949-1955 consolidation era but no source pins the year. The building survives as a private residence. SURPRISE: this row almost certainly duplicates seed rows ALL-582 (Walnut Grove School), ALL-583 (Sycamore School), and ALL-584 (Walnut Grove District No. 68) — all the same one-room school lineage; kept separate per no-silent-merge rule, recommend coordinator merge review.

name: Defiance School District
district_operator: St. Charles County common school districts; Francis Howell R-III after consolidation
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE-DISTRICT DISAMBIGUATION: no evidence of a multi-school 'Defiance School District' ever existed. The Defiance area was served by numbered St. Charles County common school districts, each operating a single one-room school (e.g. Bacon #64, Calamus Springs #65, Walnut Grove #68, Hickory Hill #69, Richmond #70 — Township 45 Range 2, per the Boone-Duden Historical Society one-room-schools history). The school physically in Defiance village was Walnut Grove School, District No. 68 ('Defiance School' was its popular name per the SHSMO Ramsay thesis). This row therefore most plausibly denotes the one-school rural district No. 68 — treated as individual_school, and effectively the same entity as ALL-593 'Defiance School' and ALL-584 'Walnut Grove District No. 68' (batch 19). Formation/dissolution dates not documented online; the area consolidated toward Francis Howell R-III by ~1949-1955 (New Melle's parallel consolidation into FHSD came in 1949 per the Boone-Duden history; Daniel Boone Elementary opened 1955). Flagged for coordinator merge review.

name: New Melle Public School
district_operator: New Melle local school district; Francis Howell R-III after 1949
school_type: Public Elementary (also ran an unaccredited first-year high school program ~1922)
notes: Seed's '1800s' resolved to 1860: the New Melle historical marker (HMDB) states '1860 - First public school was opened' and the Boone-Duden Historical Society's 'New Melle Thru the Years' (2022) states '1860 New Melle School District established - first log building,' replaced by an 1898 'modern' frame building. A 1922 Wentzville Union item cited by Boone-Duden shows the school also ran a (then-unaccredited) first-year high school program, with some pupils attending Howell High School. District consolidation came in 1949, placing New Melle in the Francis Howell School District; Daniel Boone Elementary (seed ALL-587) was dedicated in 1955 on 16 acres donated by the Meier family (191 initial pupils) per Boone-Duden, matching FHSD's official timeline 'Daniel Boone Elementary opens (1955)' and the school's own parent handbook ('first opened its doors in 1955'). Seed's 1955 close = replacement by Daniel Boone. ZIP NOTE: New Melle's actual ZIP is 63365, not 63341.

name: New Melle Parochial School 1
district_operator: St. Paul Lutheran Church or New Melle Methodist Church (unresolved)
notes: UNRESOLVED IDENTITY — generic placeholder row. Two pre-1900 parochial schools are documented for New Melle (cityofnewmelle.com city history: 'a public school, two parochial schools'; the 1874 Campbell's Gazetteer records 'three schoolhouses' with the Lutheran and Methodist churches). Per the Boone-Duden Historical Society history they were: (1) the St. Paul's Lutheran 'German school' — founded soon after the 1844 congregation, housed by the main Lutheran cemetery until a new building was dedicated on Easter Monday 1919 next to the church (this is almost certainly the same entity as seed row ALL-598 'St. Paul Lutheran School'); and (2) a Methodist school south of town (Methodist congregation est. 1869). It cannot be determined which of the two this row intends without the seed compiler's input; ALL-597 'New Melle Parochial School 2' (assigned to another batch) presumably covers the other. Recommend coordinator reconcile ALL-596/597/598 into two real rows: 'St. Paul Lutheran School' and 'New Melle Methodist (parochial) School.' No dates resolvable online; church archives (St. Paul's; Boone-Duden Historical Society) are the recommended human follow-up.

name: St. Paul Lutheran School
district_operator: St. Paul Lutheran Church (LCMS), New Melle
notes: St. Paul's Lutheran Church was founded by Melle, Germany immigrants in 1844 — the first Lutheran church in St. Charles County and a charter member of the Missouri Synod (1847) — and the Boone-Duden Historical Society history records a 'German school soon after' the founding (opened_year 1844 = 'soon after 1844,' probable, not an exact documented year). The school sat by the main Lutheran cemetery until a new school building was dedicated Easter Monday 1919 next to the church (Wentzville Union item cited by Boone-Duden). The church's NRHP listing (1982, ref 82004713) carries the alternate name 'St. Paul's Lutheran Church and Day School' — its listed 'significant year' 1965 may mark the school's end but is not confirmed. The church itself is still active (stpaulsnewmelle.com) but does not list an operating day school today, so closure is left unknown. Likely absorbed students into New Melle public schooling / Daniel Boone Elementary over time, but no citation. Church archives could supply exact open/close dates — recommended human follow-up (Boone-Duden Historical Society archives are in the Kamphoefner House, New Melle). ZIP NOTE: actual ZIP is 63365.

name: Defiance Area Rural Schools
district_operator: Multiple St. Charles County common school districts
notes: AGGREGATE PLACEHOLDER, NOT A SINGLE SCHOOL — this row covers the cluster of one-room common-school-district schools around Defiance (Township 45 Range 2, St. Charles County). Documented members from Bob Brail's 'The One-Room Schools of Township 45, Range 2' (Boone-Duden Historical Society sources) and the SHSMO Ramsay place-names thesis: Bacon School #64 (Old Colony Rd & Hwy DD; pre-1875 — closed June 2, 1950, building later burned); Calamus Springs School #65 (near Hwy 94 & DD quarry; opened 1896, closed ~1950; building still stands, N38.39.653 W90.46.209); Walnut Grove School #68 (originally Sycamore School, Darst Bottom; moved to Defiance ~1944 — same entity as ALL-593/ALL-582/583/584); Hickory Hill School #69 (1.5 mi west of Matson on Howell Rd; pre-1875 log origins; now a private residence); Richmond School #70 (Hwy F at Stub Rd; pre-1875 log origins; now a private residence); plus Mount Hope School (built ~1837, in use until the 1940s — now preserved at the Daniel Boone Home/Boonesfield Village, Defiance) and African School (Callaway Township, south of Foristell — SHSMO). Consolidation wave hit 1949-1955 (Bacon's 1950 closure and Daniel Boone Elementary's 1955 opening bracket it). Recommend the coordinator split this row into per-school rows; several are already seeded (ALL-582-584).

name: Liberty High School
notes: Seed's 2013 confirmed: the school's own site states 'Established: 2013'; the district cut the ribbon August 14, 2013 and opened with ~283 freshmen (FOX 2, Patch, St. Louis Post-Dispatch) as the Wentzville district's third high school. Physically in O'Fallon with a Lake St. Louis postal address (2275 Sommers Rd, 63367). First principal Phil Ragusky came from Frontier Middle (ALL-607), its feeder. Currently operating.

name: Timberland High School
notes: SEED YEAR WRONG (1991): the facility at 559 E Highway N opened August 28, 2000 as an annex of Wentzville Holt High School for ~400 freshmen/sophomores; the board named it Timberland High School in May 2001 (name submitted by a student) and it became a fully independent four-year high school in 2002 — per Wikipedia's detailed history, corroborated by the district homepage's '2000' year tile and publicschoolreview ('Year Founded 2002'). Address is Wentzville 63385, not 63367 — the 'Served ZIP/community' listing reflects its attendance zone covering Lake St. Louis-area residents. Currently operating.

name: Emil E. Holt Sr. High School
notes: SEED YEAR IS THE RENAME, NOT THE OPENING: 'Opened 1969' reflects the year the school was officially named for Emil E. Holt (school board member for 46 years). The underlying school — Wentzville High School — was established in 1896 as a two-year high school (first graduating class 1898, three graduates); the building burned in 1908 and was rebuilt; expanded 1938 and reorganized as a full four-year high school in 1939; moved to a new building at 405 Campus Drive in 1962; and moved to its current 600 Campus Drive building (built 1975 as the middle school) in the late 1980s. The 'Holt' name was only adopted in common use in 2000 when signage was changed ahead of the Timberland annex opening. Confidence on 1896 is 'probable' — Wikipedia's own source line carries a citation-needed flag, though the same account appears on the school paper's history page (holttribe.com). Yearbook title: 'Pow Wow' (Wikipedia infobox). FLAG: seed row ALL-604 'Wentzville High School' (in another batch) is the same school — recommend coordinator merge review. Actual ZIP 63385.

name: Wentzville Middle School
notes: Opening date is layered: the school's own homepage displays '1964' as its founding-year tile (probable — the tile is unlabeled but matches the district's established-year convention used on other school sites). The building it now occupies at 405 Campus Drive was built in 1962 as the high school per Wikipedia's Holt history, and was redesignated Wentzville Middle School only in the late 1980s when high school students moved into the expanded 1975 building — so 1964 likely marks the junior-high entity's organization rather than the building. Where the middle school was housed 1964-late-1980s not found. Actual ZIP 63385. Currently operating.

name: Wentzville South Middle School
notes: Could not pin an opening year online. Documented operating by December 2006 (St. Louis Suburban Journals honor roll, 2006-07 year). Hoener Architects documents 2012 additions. NCES lists it open (grades 6-8). Recommend checking WSD board minutes or a facilities bond history for the exact year.
